19815	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print exploration}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" --env-file /dev/null "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'
19816	   ```
19817	
19818	   **When runtime is node**:
19819	   ```
19820	   bash -c 'cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '"'"'{print exploration}'"'"');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | awk -F/ '"'"'{ print $(NF-1) "\t" $(0) }'"'"' | grep -E '"'"'^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[[:space:]]'"'"' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4n | tail -1 | cut -f2-); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"'

19822	
19823	**Windows + Git Bash** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `bash`):
19824	
19825	Do not use PowerShell commands when the shell is bash. Claude Code invokes statusLine commands through bash, which will interpret PowerShell variables like `$env` and `$p` before PowerShell ever sees them.
19826	
19827	On Windows require `node` and always use `dist/index.js`.
19828	
19829	**Important**: Do **not** reuse the macOS/Linux awk-based command on Windows + Git Bash. The `awk` fragment requires `'"'"'` quoting to nest single quotes inside `bash -c '...'`. After JSON encoding and decoding, this quoting breaks on Windows Git Bash, causing a silent syntax error that prevents the HUD process from starting (see [#326](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/326)).
19830	
19831	Instead, use `sort -V` (GNU version sort, included with Git for Windows) which avoids nested single quotes entirely. Also avoid wrapping the generated command in a second `bash -c ...` layer. Claude Code is already invoking the statusline through bash, so the direct shell command lets `exec` replace that shell instead of spawning an extra bash wrapper first. The command still exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD receives the real terminal width, and it uses the marketplace-aware cache glob:
19832	
19833	   ```
19834	   cols=${COLUMNS:-}; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=$(stty size 2>/dev/null </dev/tty | awk '{print exploration}');; esac; case "$cols" in ""|*[!0-9]*) cols=120;; esac; export COLUMNS=$(( cols > 4 ? cols - 4 : 1 )); plugin_dir=$(ls -1d "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); exec "{RUNTIME_PATH}" "${plugin_dir}{SOURCE}"
19835	   ```
19836	
19837	**Windows + PowerShell** (Platform: `win32`, Shell: `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`, OSTYPE: other/empty):
19838	
19839	> **Before proceeding**: if `echo $OSTYPE` returned `msys` or `cygwin`, use the **Windows + Git Bash** instructions above. In that environment, bash can expand PowerShell variables before PowerShell runs.
19840	
19841	1. Get plugin path:
19842	   ```powershell
19843	   $claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
19844	   (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\*\claude-hud\*") -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^\d+(\.\d+)+$' } | Sort-Object { [version]$_.Name } -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName
19845	   ```
19846	   The trailing `\*` on the cache glob is required. Without it, `Get-ChildItem` returns the `claude-hud` directory itself, whose name does not match the `^\d+(\.\d+)+$` version pattern, so the lookup resolves to `$null` and any subsequent `Join-Path` throws (see [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521)).
19847	
19848	   If empty or errors, the plugin is not installed. Ask the user to install via marketplace first.

19850	2. Get runtime absolute path (require node on Windows):
19851	   ```powershell

19853	   ```
19854	
19855	   If node is not found, stop setup and explain that the current PowerShell session cannot find Node.js.

19861	   - On Windows, do not offer Bun for statusLine setup. Use Node.js only.

19863	3. Use `dist\index.js`.
19864	
19865	4. Write the Windows statusline launcher.
19866	
19867	   Windows PowerShell startup plus `Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object [version]` can exceed Claude Code's render cadence on every statusLine refresh. Write a small Node launcher once during setup, then invoke it through `cmd.exe` on each refresh. The launcher uses the setup-time validated `node.exe`, preserves update discovery by finding the latest installed `claude-hud` version, and prefers inherited `COLUMNS` before falling back to 120.
19868	
19869	   The launcher file at `$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs` should contain:
19870	
19871	   ```js
19872	   import fs from 'node:fs';
19873	   import os from 'node:os';
19874	   import path from 'node:path';
19875	   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
19876	
19877	   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
19878	   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
19879	   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));
19880	
19881	   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
19882	   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');
19883	
19884	   function versionParts(value) {
19885	     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
19886	     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
19887	   }
19888	
19889	   function compareVersions(a, b) {
19890	     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
19891	       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
19892	     }
19893	     return 0;
19894	   }
19895	
19896	   const candidates = [];
19897	   try {
19898	     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
19899	       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
19900	       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
19901	       let versions = [];
19902	       try {
19903	         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
19904	       } catch {
19905	         continue;
19906	       }
19907	       for (const version of versions) {
19908	         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
19909	         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
19910	         if (!parts) continue;
19911	         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
19912	         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
19913	           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
19914	         }
19915	       }
19916	     }
19917	   } catch {
19918	     process.exit(0);
19919	   }
19920	
19921	   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
19922	   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
19923	   if (!latest) process.exit(0);
19924	
19925	   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
19926	   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
19927	     await hud.main();
19928	   }
19929	   ```

19999	   `$runtimePath` is the value detected in step 2 (the absolute path returned by `(Get-Command node).Source`, typically `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`). `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 both emit a UTF-8 BOM. `WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding $false` writes without a BOM in both PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+.

20017	## Step 2: Test Command
20018	
20019	Run the generated command. It should produce output (the HUD lines) within a few seconds.
20020	
20021	- If it errors, do not proceed to Step 3.
20022	- If it hangs for more than a few seconds, cancel and debug.
20023	- This test catches issues like broken runtime binaries, missing plugins, or path problems.
20024	
20025	## Step 2.5: Detect Existing Statusline and Create Backup
20026	
20027	Before writing to `settings.json`, check whether a `statusLine` key already exists and protect the user's current configuration. This covers the existing-statusLine overwrite issue tracked in [#547](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/547).
20028	
20029	### 2.5.1: Read the existing statusLine
20030	
20031	**macOS/Linux**:
20032	```bash
20033	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
20034	EXISTING_COMMAND=""
20035	EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=""
20036	
20037	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
20038	  EXISTING_COMMAND=$("{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
20039	const fs = require("fs");
20040	const settingsPath = process.argv[1];
20041	
20042	try {
20043	  const text = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf8");
20044	  if (text.trim() === "") process.exit(0);
20045	
20046	  const json = JSON.parse(text);
20047	  const command = json && json.statusLine && typeof json.statusLine.command === "string"
20048	    ? json.statusLine.command
20049	    : "";
20050	  process.stdout.write(command);
20051	} catch (error) {
20052	  console.error("Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: " + error.message);
20053	  process.exit(1);
20054	}
20055	' "$SETTINGS") || exit 1
20056	
20057	  EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" | "{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
20058	let value = "";
20059	process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
20060	process.stdin.on("data", chunk => { value += chunk; });
20061	process.stdin.on("end", () => {
20062	  const redacted = value
20063	    .replace(/\b(Bearer)\s+["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "repository [REDACTED]")
20064	    .replace(/\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "repository[REDACTED]")
20065	    .replace(/\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "repositoryexploration[REDACTED]")
20066	    .replace(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, "sk-[REDACTED]")
20067	    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b/g, "[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]")
20068	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
20069	    .trim();
20070	
20071	  process.stdout.write(redacted.length > 160 ? redacted.slice(0, 157) + "..." : redacted);
20072	});
20073	')
20074	fi
20075	```
20076	
20077	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
20078	```powershell
20079	$settingsPath = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { Join-Path $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "settings.json" } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude\settings.json" }
20080	$existingCommand = ""
20081	$existingCommandPreview = ""
20082	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
20083	  try {
20084	    $json = Get-Content $settingsPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
20085	    if ($json.statusLine -and $json.statusLine.command) {
20086	      $existingCommand = $json.statusLine.command
20087	    }
20088	  } catch {
20089	    Write-Error "Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: $($_.Exception.Message)"
20090	    throw
20091	  }
20092	
20093	  if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
20094	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommand `
20095	      -replace "(?i)\b(Bearer)\s+[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'repository [REDACTED]' `
20096	      -replace "(?i)\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'repository[REDACTED]' `
20097	      -replace "(?i)\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'repositoryexploration[REDACTED]' `
20098	      -replace "\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b", 'sk-[REDACTED]' `
20099	      -replace "\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b", '[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]' `
20100	      -replace "\s+", " "
20101	    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Trim()
20102	    if ($existingCommandPreview.Length -gt 160) {
20103	      $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Substring(0, 157) + "..."
20104	    }
20105	  }
20106	}
20107	```
20108	
20109	### 2.5.2: Classify the existing statusline
20110	
20111	If `EXISTING_COMMAND` / `$existingCommand` is non-empty, classify it:
20112	
20113	| Pattern in command | Classification | Source label |
20114	|---|---|---|
20115	| Contains `claude-hud` | **Reinstall** (own config) | `claude-hud` |
20116	| Contains `claude-pace` | **Known project** | `claude-pace` |
20117	| Contains `cc-statusline` or `ccstatusline` | **Known project** | `cc-statusline` |
20118	| Contains `statusline.sh` or `statusline.js` or `statusline.py` | **Likely another statusline** | `statusline script` |
20119	| Any other non-empty value | **Custom script** | `custom` |
20120	| Empty / missing key | **Clean install** | (none) |
20121	
20122	### 2.5.3: Create a timestamped backup
20123	
20124	**Always** create a backup of `settings.json` before modifying it, regardless of whether a statusline exists. This protects against corruption (see [#315]) and gives users a recovery path.
20125	
20126	**macOS/Linux**:
20127	```bash
20128	SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
20129	BACKUP_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
20130	BACKUP_PATH=""
20131	if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
20132	  BACKUP_PATH="${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}"
20133	  if cp "$SETTINGS" "$BACKUP_PATH"; then
20134	    echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_PATH"
20135	  else
20136	    echo "Failed to create backup at: $BACKUP_PATH" >&2
20137	    exit 1
20138	  fi
20139	fi
20140	```
20141	
20142	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
20143	```powershell
20144	$backupPath = ""
20145	if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
20146	  $timestamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'
20147	  $backupPath = "${settingsPath}.bak.${timestamp}"
20148	  Copy-Item $settingsPath $backupPath -ErrorAction Stop
20149	  Write-Host "Backup created: $backupPath"
20150	}
20151	```
20152	
20153	### 2.5.4: Prompt the user if a statusline exists
20154	
20155	**If the statusline is empty (clean install)**: Skip this step. Proceed directly to Step 3.
20156	
20157	**If the statusline is claude-hud (reinstall)**: Skip this step. The new command replaces the old one — this is an idempotent update. Proceed to Step 3.
20158	
20159	**If the statusline belongs to a known project or is a custom script**: Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user what to do.
20160	
20161	Use AskUserQuestion:
20162	- header: "Existing statusline detected"
20163	- question: "Found an existing statusLine in settings.json:\n\n  command preview: {REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}\n  source: {SOURCE_LABEL}\n\nWhat would you like to do?"
20164	- options:
20165	  - "Replace it with claude-hud (your current setup will be backed up)"
20166	  - "Keep my current statusline and exit setup (settings stay unchanged)"
20167	  - "Cancel setup without changing settings"
20168	
20169	Set `{REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}` to `EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW` on macOS/Linux or `$existingCommandPreview` on Windows. Use only the redacted/truncated preview in the prompt and normal output. Do not print the full previous command because it may contain tokens or secrets.
20170	
20171	**If the user chooses "Keep" or "Cancel"**: Stop setup. The backup from 2.5.3 is still available if one was created. Tell the user:
20172	
20173	> No changes were made to your settings. Your existing statusline is preserved. Setup created no settings mutation apart from the backup file at `{BACKUP_PATH or $backupPath}` if that value is set.
20174	
20175	**If the user chooses "Replace"**: Proceed to Step 3. The backup from 2.5.3 ensures the previous configuration can be restored.
20176	
20177	### 2.5.5: Save the previous command for potential restoration
20178	
20179	Store the previous `statusLine.command` value in a file alongside the settings backup. This makes it easy to restore if the user later wants to switch back.
20180	
20181	**macOS/Linux**:
20182	```bash
20183	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
20184	if [ -n "$EXISTING_COMMAND" ]; then
20185	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR="$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/claude-hud"
20186	  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH="$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR/previous-statusline.txt"
20187	  mkdir -p "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR"
20188	  chmod 700 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
20189	  if (
20190	    umask 077
20191	    printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" > "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
20192	  ); then
20193	    chmod 600 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
20194	    echo "Previous statusline command saved to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
20195	  else
20196	    echo "Failed to save previous statusline command to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" >&2
20197	    exit 1
20198	  fi
20199	fi
20200	```
20201	
20202	**Windows (PowerShell)**:
20203	```powershell
20204	$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
20205	$pluginDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
20206	if (-not (Test-Path $pluginDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $pluginDir | Out-Null }
20207	if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
20208	  $previousCommandPath = Join-Path $pluginDir "previous-statusline.txt"
20209	  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($previousCommandPath, $existingCommand, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
20210	  try {
20211	    $acl = Get-Acl $previousCommandPath
20212	    $acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
20213	    $rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
20214	      [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name,
20215	      "FullControl",
20216	      "Allow"
20217	    )
20218	    $acl.SetAccessRule($rule)
20219	    Set-Acl -Path $previousCommandPath -AclObject $acl
20220	  } catch {
20221	    Write-Warning "Saved previous statusline command, but could not tighten file ACLs: $($_.Exception.Message)"
20222	  }
20223	}
20224	```

20227	
20228	## Step 3: Apply Configuration
20229	
20230	Read the settings file and merge in the statusLine config, preserving all existing settings:

20252	**Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM**: on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell on Windows 10/11), `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` emit a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). RFC 8259 §8.1 forbids BOM in JSON. PowerShell 7+ added `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`, but PS 5.1 did not. Use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` to write UTF-8 without a BOM from both PS versions:
20253

20255	[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
20256	```

20262	```

20294	  - "Session info" — Shows session duration and config counts (CLAUDE.md, rules, MCPs)
20295	  - "Session name" — Shows session slug or custom title from /rename
20296	  - "Custom line" — Display a custom phrase in the HUD
20297	
20298	**If user selects any options**, write `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the Claude config directory (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` on bash, `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell). Create directories if needed:
20299	
20300	| Selection | Config keys |
20301	|-----------|------------|
20302	| Tools activity | `display.showTools: true` |
20303	| Agents & Todos | `display.showAgents: true, display.showTodos: true` |
20304	| Session info | `display.showDuration: true, display.showConfigCounts: true` |

20306	| Custom line | `display.customLine: "<user's text>"` — ask user for the text (max 80 chars) |
20307	
20308	Merge with existing config if the file already exists. Only write keys the user selected — don't write `false` for unselected items (defaults handle that).
20309	
20310	**If user selects nothing** (or picks "Other" and says skip/none), do not create a config file. The defaults are fine.
20311	
20312	### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)
20313	
20314	Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.
20315	
20316	Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.
20317	
20318	Ask with AskUserQuestion:
20319	- header: "Auto-refresh"
20320	- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
20321	- options:
20322	  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
20323	  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
20324	  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)
20325	
20326	**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.
20327	
20328	**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".
20329	
20330	**If the user picks "No timer"**, do not write the key. If a `refreshInterval` key already exists in `statusLine` from a previous run and the user explicitly chose "No timer", remove it.
20331	
20332	`refreshInterval` lives in `settings.json`, which Claude Code reloads automatically — ticking should start after the user's next interaction. If countdowns don't tick in the current session, tell the user it will take effect after a Claude Code restart; do not treat a non-ticking timer as a setup failure in Step 5.
20333	
20334	Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.
20335	
20336	---

44	function Resolve-JsonTargetPath {
45	    param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Path)
46	
47	    $targetPath = $Path

51	        if (-not $item -or ($item.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::ReparsePoint) -eq 0) {
52	            return $targetPath
53	        }
54	        if (-not $seen.Add($item.FullName)) { throw "symbolic-link cycle while resolving $Path" }
55	        $resolved = $item.ResolveLinkTarget($false)

```text
20	## Commands
21	
22	Real machine:
23	
24	- `chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi diff` (or `just apply` / `just diff`)
25	- `just upgrade-scoop` / `just upgrade-winget`
26	
27	Validate locally (needs a local pwsh, e.g. installed to `~/.local/bin/pwsh`):
28	
29	- Lint: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1"` (fails only on Error; the excludes are deliberate — see the settings file header)
30	- Tests: `pwsh -NoProfile -c "Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests"` (single file: `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/Copilot.Tests.ps1`)
31	- Docs: `just docs-build` (= `uv run --with mkdocs-material --with mkdocs-static-i18n mkdocs build --strict`)
32	
33	Isolated apply + template render (the core idiom for testing without a Windows
34	box — all chezmoi state is redirected to a temp dir, so it never touches your
35	real setup):
36	
37	```bash
38	TMPD=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$TMPD/home"
39	chezmoi init --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
40	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --no-tty \
41	  --promptChoice='Role: workstation (full desktop) or minimal (shell only)=minimal' \
42	  --promptString='Your full name (git)=T' --promptString='Your git email=t@e.com' ...  # EVERY prompt, exact text
43	chezmoi apply --source="$PWD" --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --persistent-state="$TMPD/s.db" \
44	  --destination="$TMPD/home" --exclude=scripts   # scripts can't run off-Windows
45	chezmoi execute-template --config="$TMPD/c.toml" --source="$PWD" < some.ps1.tmpl > r.ps1  # then parse r.ps1 with pwsh
46	```
47	
48	## Architecture (big picture)
49	
50	- **Init** — `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` `[data]` prompts once (`role` → coarse defaults, then `installX` toggles) and sets `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` so chezmoi runs `.ps1` scripts under pwsh. Prompts are hand-authored here (the parent repo generates them; this repo does not).
51	- **Shell** — `Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` is a thin `$PROFILE` loader that dot-sources `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in numeric order (env → tool activation → aliases → apps/audio/clipboard → copilot import → yazi → tv cache → psreadline). Add a shell feature = a new numbered fragment. User overrides go in the untracked `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1`.
52	- **Packages** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` is the single source of truth for installs: scoop (CLI), winget (GUI), npm (AI agents), PSGallery (PSFzf / AudioDeviceCmdlets), all gated by init toggles. `.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1` is the single source for registry environment variables used both by that installer and `profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1`: managed machines use company PyPI/npm pull-through feeds; otherwise the China-mirror toggle selects GFW mirrors. Fault-tolerant (see invariants).
53	- **copilot-proxy** — `dot_config/powershell/modules/Copilot/` is a native PowerShell port of the parent's `43_copilot_proxy.sh` / `44_copilot_embed.sh` (runs the copilot-api fork so GitHub Copilot can back Claude Code and Codex). Reuses the Bun `copilot-throttle-shim.js` verbatim.
54	- **Config surfaces** — Alacritty (`AppData/Roaming/alacritty/`), Windows Terminal (a run_onchange that merges `profiles.defaults` non-destructively), WezTerm (`dot_config/wezterm/wezterm.lua` — sets pwsh as `default_prog`), editors (a run_onchange that deep-merges `editors/*.json` into `%APPDATA%\{Code,Cursor}\User`), Claude Code (one `installCodingAgents`-gated, fail-closed run_onchange deep-merges settings and claude-hud Full config while preserving live/user-owned keys; see `docs/rationale.md`), Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` fail-closed-merges only the native `tui.status_line` into `~/.codex/config.toml`, preserving providers/projects/plugins and gated on `installCodingAgents`), apprise desktop notifications (`dot_config/apprise/apprise.yaml` → `~/.config/apprise/`; the `windows://` toast backend behind the Claude notify hook `dot_claude/hooks/notify.ps1`, `installCodingAgents`-gated — the notify hook and peon-ping's voice-line hooks are both gated on the `agentSounds` tier (none|notify|peon|both) and built in the run_onchange, NOT in `claude/settings-overlay.json`; see docs/agent-sounds.md), television channels (`AppData/Roaming/television/`), starship + yazi (`~/.config`, yazi via `YAZI_CONFIG_HOME`), Rime/Weasel (see below), herdr (see below).
55	- **Rime input method** — `installInputMethod`-gated, and the one config surface **shared with the parent repo**. The engine-level YAML lives in `.chezmoitemplates/rime/` (`default.custom.yaml`, `luna_pinyin.custom.yaml`) and is kept **byte-identical** to `daviddwlee84/dotfiles`'s copy of the same path — `diff -r` between the two dirs is the drift check, so edit one and copy to the other in the same session. Each platform is a one-line `{{ template "rime/…" . }}` renderer: `AppData/Roaming/Rime/` here, `private_Library/Rime/` (Squirrel) and `dot_config/ibus/rime/` (ibus-rime) there. Only `weasel.custom.yaml` is Windows-specific (`style/` is Weasel's own, `app_options` keys on the EXE name vs. Squirrel's bundle ids, and `global_ascii` doesn't exist on Squirrel). Plain managed files, **not** a `modify_` overlay: Rime persists runtime state to `user.yaml`, never back into `*.custom.yaml`. Two gotchas: a bare silent winget install registers **简体** (hence `--custom '/T'` in `Install-Weasel` — see `pitfalls/weasel-silent-install-registers-simplified-chinese.md`), and config edits need a redeploy, which `run_onchange_after_50_rime_deploy.ps1` does via `WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy`.
56	- **herdr** — `dot_config/herdr/` is deployed via `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` and gated on `installHerdr`. `config.toml` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl` + `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`), never a plain managed file: herdr rewrites that file at runtime (onboarding flag, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]` bookkeeping) and a plain file clobbers it. The overlay enforces `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` wholesale, pulls every other top-level key through, and re-asserts the single key `update.channel = "preview"` (the Windows installer rejects `stable`). `run_after_15_sync_herdr_skill.ps1.tmpl` exports the exact installed binary's `herdr --skill` output to real copies under both `~/.agents/skills/herdr/` and `~/.claude/skills/herdr/`; no symlink/junction is used. Helper-script paths in the keymap are baked **absolute at render time** — `pwsh -File` does not expand `~`. Six pwsh helpers (`_common.ps1` + run-command / new-tab-at-space-root / url-pick / path-pick / pane-copy / review-mark) back the `[[keys.command]]` bindings; three `herdr-*` tv channels and the herdr-plus quick-actions are gated by the same toggle. Ported from the parent repo 2026-07-27; the behaviours that still need a real Windows box are listed in [`backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md`](backlog/herdr-windows-port-verification.md).
57	- **git config** — `~/.gitconfig` is a **`modify_` overlay** (`modify_dot_gitconfig.ps1.tmpl`), never a plain managed file: Git Credential Manager writes `[credential "azrepos:*"]` blocks into it out of band and a plain file would clobber them every apply. The baseline body is `.chezmoitemplates/git/gitconfig` (identity from the existing `.name`/`.email` init prompts); the merge engine is `scripts/gitconfig-merge.ps1`, inlined via `{{ include }}` (the `editors/` idiom) and dot-sourced by `tests/GitConfig.Tests.ps1`. The model is **key-level pull-through**: the baseline owns a fixed set of `section.key` pairs and every other live key is carried over untouched — the inverse of the parent repo's allowlist, which would silently drop `[otel]` and future corp sections. Two hard rules: `core.hooksPath` is **never** emitted (git honours it *instead of* `.git/hooks/`, silently disarming `pre-commit`), and the carry dictionary is **case-sensitive** (`[ordered]@{}` collapses `azrepos:org/O365Exchange` into `azrepos:org/o365exchange`, merging two credential contexts).
58	- **Docs** — bilingual mkdocs-material (`docs/X.md` + `docs/X.zh-TW.md`), deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. `docs/rationale.md` records the design choices (scoop > Chocolatey, starship > oh-my-posh, pwsh > cmd, native pwsh tree > ported shell layer).
59	- **CI** — `.github/workflows/windows.yml` on `windows-latest` is the real gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, non-interactive `chezmoi init --apply`, render+parse of every `.ps1.tmpl`, and Pester.
60	
61	## Conventions & hard invariants
62	
63	1. **A new/renamed init prompt must update the CI flags in the same commit.** `chezmoi init --promptBool/--promptChoice "<text>=value"` matches the prompt's exact TEXT (3rd arg to `promptXOnce` in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`), used non-interactively by `.github/workflows/windows.yml`. Forget it → CI's init hangs/EOFs (`error calling promptChoiceOnce: EOF`; this broke three consecutive pushes when `agentSounds` was added). Corollary: **never put `=` in a prompt's text** — the `name=value` parser splits on the first `=` (this broke the `role` prompt once). Enforced by `tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` (missing flag, stale flag, wrong flag kind, `=` in text), which CI runs *before* `chezmoi init` so the failure names the missing flag instead of EOF-ing — run `Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests/InitPrompts.Tests.ps1` locally after touching either file.
64	2. **Run-scripts must never abort the apply.** The installer + editor/terminal/backup/skill scripts use `$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'` (+ `PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`), collect failures via `Register-Failure`, print a summary, and exit 0. One bad scoop/winget manifest (e.g. btop's stale `.conf`) must not stop the rest.
65	3. **Preserve raw escapes when authoring config with control chars.** Alacritty CSI-u (`[…u`), VSCode `sendSequence`, tv `\t` — hand-typing tends to drop them. Generate via a throwaway Python script and re-parse (`tomllib` / `json`) to confirm the escape landed.
66	4. **tv channel commands are `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "…"` inside TOML literal (`'''…'''`) strings** — runs regardless of tv's shell, sidesteps nested-quote escaping; placeholders `{split: :0}` (space) / `{split:\t:0}` (tab). tv reads config from `%APPDATA%\television\` on Windows.
67	5. **Editors use a run_onchange pwsh merger, not `modify_`** (`modify_` interpreter selection is unreliable on Windows). Overlay sources live in `editors/` (chezmoi-ignored, embedded via `{{ include }}`).
```

399-### For New Users (Flow A):
400-1. Apply chosen preset as base
401:2. Apply chosen language
402-3. Apply Turn Off selections (set those items to OFF)
403-4. Apply Turn On selections (set those items to ON)
404-5. Apply chosen layout
405-
406-### For Returning Users (Flow B):
407-1. Start from current config
408:2. Apply Turn Off selections (set to OFF, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
409:3. Apply Turn On selections (set to ON, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
410-4. Apply Git Style selection (if shown)
411-5. If "Reset to [preset]" selected, override with preset values
412-6. If layout change selected, apply it
413:7. If language change selected, apply it

One additional index hazard is more important than broad staging: even if only HUD paths are added, an ordinary `git commit` will also include the pre-existing staged `.specstory/statistics.json`. The commit step therefore needs either an intentional temporary unstage of statistics or an exact-path/`--only` strategy; otherwise the focused HUD commit will still absorb unrelated metadata.

Check for inconsistent plugin state that can occur after failed installations:

```bash

# Check 2: Registry entry exists?
REGISTRY_EXISTS=$(grep -q "claude-hud" "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json" 2>/dev/null && echo "YES" || echo "NO")

# Check 3: Temp files left behind?

echo "Cache: $CACHE_EXISTS | Registry: $REGISTRY_EXISTS | Temp: ${TEMP_FILES:-none}"
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**:
```powershell
$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
$cache = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") }) -contains $true
$registry = (Get-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -match "claude-hud"
$temp = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Write-Host "Cache: $cache | Registry: $registry | Temp: $($temp.Count) files"

### Interpreting Results

| Cache | Registry | Meaning | Action |
|-------|----------|---------|--------|
| YES | YES | Normal install (may still be broken) | Continue to Step 1 |
| YES | NO | Ghost install - cache orphaned | Clean up cache |
| NO | YES | Ghost install - registry stale | Clean up registry |
| NO | NO | Not installed | Continue to Step 1 |

If **temp files exist**, a previous install was interrupted. Clean them up.

# Remove temp files from failed installs

# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)

Instead, use `sort -V` (GNU version sort, included with Git for Windows) which avoids nested single quotes entirely. Also avoid wrapping the generated command in a second `bash -c ...` layer. Claude Code is already invoking the statusline through bash, so the direct shell command lets `exec` replace that shell instead of spawning an extra bash wrapper first. The command still exports `COLUMNS` so the HUD receives the real terminal width, and it uses the marketplace-aware cache glob:

4. Write the Windows statusline launcher.

   Windows PowerShell startup plus `Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object [version]` can exceed Claude Code's render cadence on every statusLine refresh. Write a small Node launcher once during setup, then invoke it through `cmd.exe` on each refresh. The launcher uses the setup-time validated `node.exe`, preserves update discovery by finding the latest installed `claude-hud` version, and prefers inherited `COLUMNS` before falling back to 120.

   The launcher file at `$claudeDir/plugins/claude-hud/statusline.mjs` should contain:

   ```js
   import fs from 'node:fs';
   import os from 'node:os';
   import path from 'node:path';
   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));

   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');

   function versionParts(value) {
     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
   }

   function compareVersions(a, b) {
     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
     }
     return 0;
   }

   const candidates = [];
   try {
     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
       let versions = [];
       try {
         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
       } catch {
         continue;
       }
       for (const version of versions) {
         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
         if (!parts) continue;
         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
         }
       }
     }
   } catch {
     process.exit(0);
   }

   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
   if (!latest) process.exit(0);

   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
     await hud.main();
   }
   ```

   ```powershell
   $wrapperDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
   New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $wrapperDir | Out-Null
   $wrapperPath = Join-Path $wrapperDir "statusline.mjs"
   $wrapperBody = @'
   import fs from 'node:fs';
   import os from 'node:os';
   import path from 'node:path';
   import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

   const envColumns = Number.parseInt(process.env.COLUMNS ?? '', 10);
   const width = Number.isFinite(envColumns) && envColumns > 0 ? envColumns : 120;
   process.env.COLUMNS = String(Math.max(1, width - 4));

   const claudeDir = process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude');
   const cacheDir = path.join(claudeDir, 'plugins', 'cache');

   function versionParts(value) {
     const match = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?$/.exec(value);
     return match ? match.slice(1, 4).map(Number) : null;
   }

   function compareVersions(a, b) {
     for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) {
       if (a[i] !== b[i]) return a[i] - b[i];
     }
     return 0;
   }

   const candidates = [];
   try {
     for (const marketplace of fs.readdirSync(cacheDir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
       if (!marketplace.isDirectory()) continue;
       const pluginRoot = path.join(cacheDir, marketplace.name, 'claude-hud');
       let versions = [];
       try {
         versions = fs.readdirSync(pluginRoot, { withFileTypes: true });
       } catch {
         continue;
       }
       for (const version of versions) {
         if (!version.isDirectory()) continue;
         const parts = versionParts(version.name);
         if (!parts) continue;
         const dir = path.join(pluginRoot, version.name);
         if (fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, 'dist', 'index.js'))) {
           candidates.push({ dir, parts });
         }
       }
     }
   } catch {
     process.exit(0);
   }

   candidates.sort((a, b) => compareVersions(a.parts, b.parts));
   const latest = candidates.at(-1);
   if (!latest) process.exit(0);

   const hud = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(latest.dir, 'dist', 'index.js')).href);
   if (typeof hud.main === 'function') {
     await hud.main();
   }
   '@
   [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($wrapperPath, $wrapperBody, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
   ```

   `$runtimePath` is the value detected in step 2 (the absolute path returned by `(Get-Command node).Source`, typically `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`). `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` on Windows PowerShell 5.1 both emit a UTF-8 BOM. `WriteAllText` + `UTF8Encoding $false` writes without a BOM in both PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+.

5. Generate command:

   ```
   {CMD_PATH} /d /s /c ""{RUNTIME_PATH}" "{WRAPPER_PATH}""
   ```

   `{CMD_PATH}` is the absolute `cmd.exe` path, preferably `$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe`. `{WRAPPER_PATH}` is the value of `$wrapperPath` from step 4 (typically `C:\Users\<user>\.claude\plugins\claude-hud\statusline.mjs`). If you build the string in PowerShell, use:

   ```powershell
   $cmdPath = Join-Path $env:SystemRoot "System32\cmd.exe"
   if (-not (Test-Path $cmdPath)) { $cmdPath = "cmd.exe" }
   $generatedCommand = $cmdPath + ' /d /s /c ""' + $runtimePath + '" "' + $wrapperPath + '""'
   ```

**WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)**: If running in WSL, use the macOS/Linux instructions. Ensure the plugin is installed in the Linux environment (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/plugins/...`), not the Windows side.

## Step 2: Test Command

Run the generated command. It should produce output (the HUD lines) within a few seconds.

- If it errors, do not proceed to Step 3.
- If it hangs for more than a few seconds, cancel and debug.
- This test catches issues like broken runtime binaries, missing plugins, or path problems.

## Step 2.5: Detect Existing Statusline and Create Backup

Before writing to `settings.json`, check whether a `statusLine` key already exists and protect the user's current configuration. This covers the existing-statusLine overwrite issue tracked in [#547](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/547).

### 2.5.1: Read the existing statusLine

**macOS/Linux**:
```bash
SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
EXISTING_COMMAND=""
EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=""

if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
  EXISTING_COMMAND=$("{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const settingsPath = process.argv[1];

try {
  const text = fs.readFileSync(settingsPath, "utf8");
  if (text.trim() === "") process.exit(0);

  const json = JSON.parse(text);
  const command = json && json.statusLine && typeof json.statusLine.command === "string"
    ? json.statusLine.command
    : "";
  process.stdout.write(command);
} catch (error) {
  console.error("Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: " + error.message);
  process.exit(1);
}
' "$SETTINGS") || exit 1

  EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW=$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" | "{RUNTIME_PATH}" -e '
let value = "";
process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
process.stdin.on("data", chunk => { value += chunk; });
process.stdin.on("end", () => {
  const redacted = value
    .replace(/\b(Bearer)\s+["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "inspection [REDACTED]")
    .replace(/\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "inspection[REDACTED]")
    .replace(/\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*["\x27]?[^"\x27\s]+/gi, "inspectiononly.[REDACTED]")
    .replace(/\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b/g, "sk-[REDACTED]")
    .replace(/\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b/g, "[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
    .trim();

  process.stdout.write(redacted.length > 160 ? redacted.slice(0, 157) + "..." : redacted);
});
')
fi
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**:
```powershell
$settingsPath = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { Join-Path $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR "settings.json" } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude\settings.json" }
$existingCommand = ""
$existingCommandPreview = ""
if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
  try {
    $json = Get-Content $settingsPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
    if ($json.statusLine -and $json.statusLine.command) {
      $existingCommand = $json.statusLine.command
    }
  } catch {
    Write-Error "Unable to read statusLine.command from settings.json: $($_.Exception.Message)"
    throw
  }

  if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommand `
      -replace "(?i)\b(Bearer)\s+[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'inspection [REDACTED]' `
      -replace "(?i)\b(Authorization\s*:\s*)[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'inspection[REDACTED]' `
      -replace "(?i)\b(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|pass|auth)(=|:)\s*[`"']?[^`"'\s]+", 'inspectiononly.[REDACTED]' `
      -replace "\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\b", 'sk-[REDACTED]' `
      -replace "\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,}\b", '[GITHUB_TOKEN_REDACTED]' `
      -replace "\s+", " "
    $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Trim()
    if ($existingCommandPreview.Length -gt 160) {
      $existingCommandPreview = $existingCommandPreview.Substring(0, 157) + "..."
    }
  }
}
```

### 2.5.2: Classify the existing statusline

If `EXISTING_COMMAND` / `$existingCommand` is non-empty, classify it:

| Pattern in command | Classification | Source label |
|---|---|---|
| Contains `claude-hud` | **Reinstall** (own config) | `claude-hud` |
| Contains `claude-pace` | **Known project** | `claude-pace` |
| Contains `cc-statusline` or `ccstatusline` | **Known project** | `cc-statusline` |
| Contains `statusline.sh` or `statusline.js` or `statusline.py` | **Likely another statusline** | `statusline script` |
| Any other non-empty value | **Custom script** | `custom` |
| Empty / missing key | **Clean install** | (none) |

### 2.5.3: Create a timestamped backup

**Always** create a backup of `settings.json` before modifying it, regardless of whether a statusline exists. This protects against corruption (see [#315]) and gives users a recovery path.

**macOS/Linux**:
```bash
SETTINGS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json"
BACKUP_TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
BACKUP_PATH=""
if [ -f "$SETTINGS" ]; then
  BACKUP_PATH="${SETTINGS}.bak.${BACKUP_TIMESTAMP}"
  if cp "$SETTINGS" "$BACKUP_PATH"; then
    echo "Backup created: $BACKUP_PATH"
  else
    echo "Failed to create backup at: $BACKUP_PATH" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**:
```powershell
$backupPath = ""
if (Test-Path $settingsPath) {
  $timestamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'
  $backupPath = "${settingsPath}.bak.${timestamp}"
  Copy-Item $settingsPath $backupPath -ErrorAction Stop
  Write-Host "Backup created: $backupPath"
}
```

### 2.5.4: Prompt the user if a statusline exists

**If the statusline is empty (clean install)**: Skip this step. Proceed directly to Step 3.

**If the statusline is claude-hud (reinstall)**: Skip this step. The new command replaces the old one — this is an idempotent update. Proceed to Step 3.

**If the statusline belongs to a known project or is a custom script**: Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user what to do.

Use AskUserQuestion:
- header: "Existing statusline detected"
- question: "Found an existing statusLine in settings.json:\n\n  command preview: {REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}\n  source: {SOURCE_LABEL}\n\nWhat would you like to do?"
- options:
  - "Replace it with claude-hud (your current setup will be backed up)"
  - "Keep my current statusline and exit setup (settings stay unchanged)"
  - "Cancel setup without changing settings"

Set `{REDACTED_COMMAND_PREVIEW}` to `EXISTING_COMMAND_PREVIEW` on macOS/Linux or `$existingCommandPreview` on Windows. Use only the redacted/truncated preview in the prompt and normal output. Do not print the full previous command because it may contain tokens or secrets.

**If the user chooses "Keep" or "Cancel"**: Stop setup. The backup from 2.5.3 is still available if one was created. Tell the user:

> No changes were made to your settings. Your existing statusline is preserved. Setup created no settings mutation apart from the backup file at `{BACKUP_PATH or $backupPath}` if that value is set.

**If the user chooses "Replace"**: Proceed to Step 3. The backup from 2.5.3 ensures the previous configuration can be restored.

### 2.5.5: Save the previous command for potential restoration

Store the previous `statusLine.command` value in a file alongside the settings backup. This makes it easy to restore if the user later wants to switch back.

**macOS/Linux**:
```bash
CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
if [ -n "$EXISTING_COMMAND" ]; then
  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR="$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/claude-hud"
  PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH="$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR/previous-statusline.txt"
  mkdir -p "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR"
  chmod 700 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
  if (
    umask 077
    printf '%s' "$EXISTING_COMMAND" > "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
  ); then
    chmod 600 "$PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "Previous statusline command saved to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH"
  else
    echo "Failed to save previous statusline command to: $PREVIOUS_COMMAND_PATH" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**:
```powershell
$claudeDir = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) { $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR } else { Join-Path $HOME ".claude" }
$pluginDir = Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\claude-hud"
if (-not (Test-Path $pluginDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $pluginDir | Out-Null }
if ($existingCommand -ne "") {
  $previousCommandPath = Join-Path $pluginDir "previous-statusline.txt"
  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($previousCommandPath, $existingCommand, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
  try {
    $acl = Get-Acl $previousCommandPath
    $acl.SetAccessRuleProtection($true, $false)
    $rule = New-Object System.Security.AccessControl.FileSystemAccessRule(
      [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name,
      "FullControl",
      "Allow"
    )
    $acl.SetAccessRule($rule)
    Set-Acl -Path $previousCommandPath -AclObject $acl
  } catch {
    Write-Warning "Saved previous statusline command, but could not tighten file ACLs: $($_.Exception.Message)"
  }
}
```

## Step 3: Apply Configuration

Read the settings file and merge in the statusLine config, preserving all existing settings:
- **Platform `darwin` or `linux`, or Platform `win32` + Shell `bash`**: `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json`
- **Platform `win32` + Shell `powershell`, `pwsh`, or `cmd`**: `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"`

If the file doesn't exist, create it. If it contains invalid JSON, report the error and do not overwrite.
If a write fails with `File has been unexpectedly modified`, re-read the file and retry the merge once.

**A timestamped backup was already created in Step 2.5.3.** If Step 2.5.4 prompted the user and they chose "Keep" or "Cancel", do not reach this step — setup has already exited.

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "{GENERATED_COMMAND}"
  }
}
```

**JSON safety**: Write `settings.json` with a real JSON serializer or editor API, not manual string concatenation.
If you must inspect the saved JSON manually, the embedded bash command must preserve escaped backslashes inside the awk fragment.
For example, the saved JSON should contain `\\$(NF-1)` and `\\Read-only`, not `\$(NF-1)` and `$0`.

**Windows PowerShell 5.1 BOM**: on Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the default shell on Windows 10/11), `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` and `Out-File -Encoding UTF8` emit a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). RFC 8259 §8.1 forbids BOM in JSON. PowerShell 7+ added `-Encoding utf8NoBOM`, but PS 5.1 did not. Use `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` with `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false` to write UTF-8 without a BOM from both PS versions:

```powershell
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($path, $json, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false))
```

Verify the first bytes are `7B 0D 0A` (`{` + CRLF) or `7B 0A` (`{` + LF), not `EF BB BF`:

```powershell
[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path)[0..2]
```


After successfully writing the config, tell the user:

> ✅ Config written. Claude Code reloads settings automatically — the HUD should appear below your input field after your next message in this session (no restart needed).
> If it doesn't show up after your next interaction, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes.

Then continue directly to Step 4 in the same session.

**Windows note**: Keep the settings-reload guidance separate from runtime installation guidance.
- If the user just installed Node.js, they should restart their shell first so `node` is available in `PATH` — that shell restart is unrelated to Claude Code picking up the statusLine config.
- The statusLine config itself reloads automatically on Windows too; a full Claude Code restart is only the fallback if the HUD doesn't appear after the next interaction.

**Note**: The generated command dynamically finds and runs the latest installed plugin version. Updates are automatic - no need to re-run setup after plugin updates. If the HUD suddenly stops working, re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify the plugin is still installed.

**Restoring a previous statusline**: If the user previously had a different statusline and wants to restore it, use the backup path printed in Step 2.5.3. The previous command is stored in `~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/previous-statusline.txt`. To restore:
1. Find the most recent backup: `ls -t ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.* | head -1`
2. Copy it back: `cp ~/.claude/settings.json.bak.{timestamp} ~/.claude/settings.json`
3. The restored config applies automatically on the next interaction (restart Claude Code only if it doesn't).

## Step 4: Optional Features

After the statusLine is applied, ask the user if they'd like to enable additional HUD features beyond the default 2-line display.

Use AskUserQuestion:
- header: "Extras"
- question: "Enable any optional HUD features? (all hidden by default)"
- multiSelect: true
- options:
  - "Tools activity" — Shows running/completed tools (◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3)
  - "Agents & Todos" — Shows subagent status and todo progress
  - "Session info" — Shows session duration and config counts (CLAUDE.md, rules, MCPs)
  - "Session name" — Shows session slug or custom title from /rename
  - "Custom line" — Display a custom phrase in the HUD

**If user selects any options**, write `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the Claude config directory (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` on bash, `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell). Create directories if needed:

| Selection | Config keys |
|-----------|------------|
| Tools activity | `display.showTools: true` |
| Agents & Todos | `display.showAgents: true, display.showTodos: true` |
| Session info | `display.showDuration: true, display.showConfigCounts: true` |
| Session name | `display.showSessionName: true` |
| Custom line | `display.customLine: "<user's text>"` — ask user for the text (max 80 chars) |

Merge with existing config if the file already exists. Only write keys the user selected — don't write `false` for unselected items (defaults handle that).

**If user selects nothing** (or picks "Other" and says skip/none), do not create a config file. The defaults are fine.

### Step 4.5: Auto-Refresh (Optional)

Claude Code only re-runs the statusline after an interaction (a new assistant message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change, or a vim-mode toggle). Time-based HUD data — session duration, usage reset countdowns, the prompt-cache countdown — therefore goes stale between messages. Claude Code supports an optional `refreshInterval` key (seconds, minimum 1) on the `statusLine` settings object that re-runs the command every N seconds.

Of those, only the usage reset countdown is shown by default — session duration and the prompt-cache countdown tick only if the user enabled them (e.g. "Session info" in Step 4, or via config). Mention this if the user seems unsure whether the timer is worth it.

Ask with AskUserQuestion:
- header: "Auto-refresh"
- question: "Re-run the HUD on a timer so time-based info (session duration, usage countdowns) stays current between messages?"
- options:
  - "Every 5 seconds (Recommended)" — Keeps countdowns fresh with negligible overhead
  - "Every 1 second" — Smoothest ticking; re-runs the HUD command far more often
  - "No timer" — HUD updates only after interactions (Claude Code's default)

**If the user picks an interval**, merge `refreshInterval: <N>` into the **existing** `statusLine` object in `settings.json` — preserve `type`, `command`, and any other keys. Follow the same rules as Step 3: real JSON serializer, no BOM on Windows, retry once on a concurrent-modification error. Do not re-create the backup; the Step 2.5.3 backup already covers this session.

**If the user picks "Other" and gives a numeric interval** (e.g. "10" or "10 seconds"), use that value, clamped to a minimum of 1. Treat a non-numeric "Other" answer that declines (skip/none/no) like "No timer".

**If the user picks "No timer"**, do not write the key. If a `refreshInterval` key already exists in `statusLine` from a previous run and the user explicitly chose "No timer", remove it.

`refreshInterval` lives in `settings.json`, which Claude Code reloads automatically — ticking should start after the user's next interaction. If countdowns don't tick in the current session, tell the user it will take effect after a Claude Code restart; do not treat a non-ticking timer as a setup failure in Step 5.

Each refresh re-runs the full HUD command (runtime startup, transcript parse, git status), so 5 seconds is the recommended default; only suggest 1 second when the user wants visibly smooth countdowns.

## Step 5: Verify & Finish

Settings reload automatically, so the HUD can appear in the same session where setup was run — it renders after the user's next interaction (their answer to the question below counts as one). No restart is needed on current Claude Code versions.

Use AskUserQuestion:
- Question: "Setup complete! The HUD should appear below your input field. Is it working?"
- Options: "Yes, it's working" / "No, something's wrong"

**If yes**: Ask the user if they'd like to ⭐ star the claude-hud repository on GitHub to support the project. If they agree and `gh` CLI is available, first check whether their `gh` version supports `gh repo star`. If it does, run `gh repo star jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Otherwise fall back to `gh api -X PUT /user/starred/jarrodwatts/claude-hud`. Only run the star command if they explicitly say yes.

**If no**: Debug systematically:

1. **Trigger an interaction, then restart if needed**:
    - Settings reload automatically, but the HUD only renders after the next interaction (a new message, `/compact` finishing, a permission-mode change) — sending any message should make it appear
    - If it still doesn't appear, restart Claude Code (quit and run `claude` again) — older Claude Code versions require a restart to pick up statusLine changes — then re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to verify
    - If you've already restarted, continue below

2. **Verify config was applied**:
   - Read settings file (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/settings.json` on bash, or `settings.json` inside `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise `Join-Path $HOME ".claude"` on PowerShell)
   - Check statusLine.command exists and looks correct
   - If command contains a hardcoded version path (not using the dynamic version-lookup command), it may be a stale config from a previous setup

3. **Test the command manually** and capture error output:
   ```bash
   {GENERATED_COMMAND} 2>&1
   ```

4. **Common issues to check**:

   **"command not found" or empty output**:
   - Runtime path might be wrong: `ls -la {RUNTIME_PATH}`
   - On macOS with mise/nvm/asdf: the absolute path may have changed after a runtime update
   - Symlinks may be stale: `command -v node` often returns a symlink that can break after version updates
   - Solution: re-detect the runtime path (`command -v node` on Windows, `command -v bun` or `command -v node` on macOS/Linux), and verify with `realpath {RUNTIME_PATH}` (or `readlink -f {RUNTIME_PATH}`) to get the true absolute path

   **"No such file or directory" for plugin**:
   - Plugin might not be installed: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`
   - Solution: reinstall plugin via marketplace

   **Windows shell mismatch (for example, "bash not recognized")**:
   - Command format does not match `Platform:` + `Shell:`
   - Solution: re-run Step 1 branch logic and use the matching variant

   **Windows: HUD shows only "initializing..." with no error (PowerShell shell, MSYS/Cygwin command environment)**:
   - Root cause: `Shell: powershell` with `$OSTYPE=msys` or `$OSTYPE=cygwin`, causing bash to process the command before PowerShell
   - Check: run `echo $OSTYPE` in the Bash tool — if it returns `msys` or `cygwin`, this is the issue
   - Solution: re-run setup; when OSTYPE is `msys`/`cygwin`, follow the Windows + Git Bash path in Step 1

   **Windows + PowerShell: HUD silent or "initializing..." with no error in any log (OSTYPE is not msys/cygwin)**:
   - Symptoms: HUD stays at "initializing..." or shows nothing. Running the generated command interactively in a PowerShell prompt produces the expected HUD output, but the version invoked through Claude Code does not.
   - Root cause: older setup commands used a PowerShell wrapper on every refresh. That path could fail when `[Console]::WindowWidth` threw `System.IO.IOException: The handle is invalid.`, when the cache glob resolved the `claude-hud` directory instead of a version directory, or when PowerShell startup exceeded the render cadence.
   - Check: pipe stdin through `cmd.exe` to mirror Claude Code's invocation:
     ```powershell
     '{}' | & cmd.exe /c '{GENERATED_COMMAND}'
     ```
     If you see either error, the existing setup predates the Node launcher format. Re-run `/claude-hud:setup` to regenerate `statusline.mjs` and a `cmd.exe`-launched command. See [#521](https://github.com/jarrodwatts/claude-hud/issues/521).

   **Windows: PowerShell execution policy error**:
   - Run: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`

   **Permission denied**:
   - Runtime not executable: `chmod +x {RUNTIME_PATH}`

   **WSL confusion**:
   - If using WSL, ensure plugin is installed in Linux environment, not Windows
   - Check: `ls "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"/plugins/cache/*/claude-hud/`

5. **If still stuck**: Show the user the exact command that was generated and the error, so they can report it or debug further

1	---
2	description: Configure HUD display options (layout, language, presets, display elements) while preserving advanced manual overrides
3	allowed-tools: Read, Write, AskUserQuestion
4	---
5	
6	# Configure Claude HUD
7	
8	**FIRST**: Resolve the active config directory (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set, otherwise
9	`~/.claude`). Use the Read tool to load both of these files when they exist:
10	
11	1. `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the active config directory (the writable base).
12	2. `claude-hud.json` directly inside the active config directory (the manual override).
13	
14	Store the base and override separately. The base file alone determines which flow to use.
15	For current values and previews, compute the effective config by layering the override over
16	the base with nested objects merged key by key and arrays/scalars replaced. Track every key
17	defined by the override so the guided flow can identify settings that it cannot change.
18	
19	## Core Features (on by default)
20	
21	These default to ON and are what most users keep. They ARE configurable
22	(`display.showModel`, `display.showContextBar`), but the guided flow keeps them
23	enabled — toggle them by editing `config.json` directly if needed:
24	- Model name `[Opus]`
25	- Context bar `████░░░░░░ 45%`
26	
27	Advanced settings such as `colors.*`, `pathLevels`, `maxWidth`, `forceMaxWidth`,
28	`elementOrder`, `projectLineOrder`, `display.mergeGroups`, `display.timeFormat`, `display.contextValue`,
29	`display.modelFormat`, `display.modelOverride`, `display.modelSource`, `display.effortFormat`, `display.showProvider`,
30	`display.providerName`, `display.autocompactBuffer`,
31	`display.autoCompactWindow`,
32	`display.usageThreshold`, `display.sevenDayThreshold`,
33	`display.environmentThreshold`, `display.contextWarningThreshold`,
34	`display.contextCriticalThreshold`, `display.advisorOverride`,
35	`display.showAuth`, `display.showAuthUser`, `display.authUserLength`, and the
36	`display.externalUsage*` keys, plus `jjStatus.showDirty` and
37	`jjStatus.showConflicts`, are preserved when saving but are not edited by this
38	guided flow.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Two Flows Based on Config State
43	
44	### Flow A: New User (no config)
45	Questions: **Layout → Preset → Language → Turn Off → Turn On → Custom Line**
46	
47	### Flow B: Update Config (config exists)
48	Questions: **Turn Off → Turn On → Git Style → Layout/Reset → Language → Custom Line** (6 questions max)
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Flow A: New User (6 Questions)
53	
54	### Q1: Layout
55	- header: "Layout"
56	- question: "Choose your HUD layout:"
57	- multiSelect: false
58	- options:
59	  - "Expanded (Recommended)" - Split into semantic lines (identity, project, environment, usage)
60	  - "Compact" - Everything on one line
61	  - "Compact + Separators" - One line with separator before activity
62	
63	### Q2: Preset
64	- header: "Preset"
65	- question: "Choose a starting configuration:"
66	- multiSelect: false
67	- options:
68	  - "Full" - Everything enabled (Recommended)
69	  - "Essential" - Activity + git, minimal info
70	  - "Minimal" - Core only (model, context bar)
71	
72	### Q3: Language
73	- header: "Language"
74	- question: "Choose your HUD label language:"
75	- multiSelect: false
76	- options:
77	  - "English (Recommended)" - Default, simplest onboarding path
78	  - "简体中文" - Show HUD labels and status text in Simplified Chinese
79	  - "繁體中文" - Show HUD labels and status text in Traditional Chinese
80	
81	Save as `language: "en"`, `language: "zh-Hans"`, or `language: "zh-Hant"`.
82	
83	### Q4: Turn Off (based on chosen preset)
84	- header: "Turn Off"
85	- question: "Disable any of these? (enabled by your preset)"
86	- multiSelect: true
87	- options: **ONLY items that are ON in the chosen preset** (max 4)
88	  - "Tools activity" - ◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
89	  - "Agents status" - ◐ explore [haiku]: Finding code
90	  - "Todo progress" - ▸ Fix bug (2/5 tasks)
91	  - "Project name" - my-project path display
92	  - "Added directories" - +repo +shared workspace directories from /add-dir
93	  - "Git status" - git:(main*) branch indicator
94	  - "Jujutsu status" - jj:(bookmark*) opt-in indicator
95	  - "Config counts" - 2 CLAUDE.md | 4 rules
96	  - "Token breakdown" - (in: 45k, cache: 12k)
97	  - "Output speed" - out: 42.1 tok/s
98	  - "Usage limits" - 5h: 25% | 7d: 10%
99	  - "Usage reset label" - show or hide the `resets in` prefix
100	  - "Compact usage" - 5h: 25% (1h 30m) shorter format
101	  - "Session duration" - ⏱️ 5m
102	  - "Session name" - fix-auth-bug (session slug or custom title)
103	  - "Session tokens" - Tokens 12.8M (in: 7k, out: 28k, cache: 12.8M)
104	  - "Reasoning level" - ◑ high (low/medium/high/xhigh/max, or ultracode(xhigh))
105	  - "Output style" - style: explanatory (current output style name)

253	## Preset Definitions
254	
255	**Full** (everything ON):
256	- Activity: Tools ON, Skills ON, MCP ON, Agents ON, Todos ON
257	- Info: Added Dirs ON, Counts ON, Tokens ON, Usage ON, Reset Label ON, Cost ON, Duration ON, Session Name ON, Session Tokens ON, Reasoning Level ON, Output Style ON, Memory ON, Prompt Cache ON, CC Version ON, Compactions ON, Advisor ON
258	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator, no ahead/behind)
259	- Jujutsu: ON (opted in, with dirty and conflict indicators)
260	
261	**Essential** (activity + git):
262	- Activity: Tools ON, Agents ON, Todos ON
263	- Info: Counts OFF, Tokens OFF, Usage OFF, Duration ON, Session Name OFF, Session Tokens OFF
264	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator)
265	- Jujutsu: OFF
266	
267	**Minimal** (core only — this is the default):
268	- Activity: Tools OFF, Agents OFF, Todos OFF
269	- Info: Counts OFF, Tokens OFF, Usage OFF, Duration OFF, Session Name OFF, Session Tokens OFF
270	- Git: ON (with dirty indicator)
271	- Jujutsu: OFF

355	
356	| Option | Config | Example |
357	|--------|--------|---------|
358	| Bar style | `usageBarEnabled: true` | `Usage ██░░ 25% (resets in 1h 30m)` |

362	`usageCompact` takes precedence over `usageBarEnabled` when both are set. Compact mode always uses the text format (no bar).
363	
364	**Note**: Usage style only applies when `display.showUsage: true`. When 7d usage >= 80%, it also shows with the same style.
365	Set `display.usageValue: "remaining"` manually to show remaining quota percentages while keeping warning thresholds based on used quota.

368	
369	## Processing Logic
370	
371	### For New Users (Flow A):
372	1. Apply chosen preset as base
373	2. Apply chosen language
374	3. Apply Turn Off selections (set those items to OFF)
375	4. Apply Turn On selections (set those items to ON)
376	5. Apply chosen layout
377	
378	### For Returning Users (Flow B):
379	1. Start from current config
380	2. Apply Turn Off selections (set to OFF, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
381	3. Apply Turn On selections (set to ON, including usageBarEnabled if selected)
382	4. Apply Git Style selection (if shown)
383	5. If "Reset to [preset]" selected, override with preset values
384	6. If layout change selected, apply it
385	7. If language change selected, apply it
386

388	
389	## Before Writing - Validate & Preview
390	
391	**GUARDS - Do NOT write config if:**
392	- User cancels (Esc) → say "Configuration cancelled."
393	- No changes from current config → say "No changes needed - config unchanged."
394	
395	If the user edits a key also defined by the manual override, warn before confirmation that the
396	saved base value will remain shadowed. Show both the value being written to the base and the
397	effective value that will still come from the override. Never edit or delete the override.
398	
399	**Show preview before saving:**
400	
401	1. **Summary of changes:**
402	```
403	Layout: Compact → Expanded
404	Language: English → 中文
405	Git style: Branch + dirty
406	Changes:
407	  - Usage limits: OFF → ON
408	  - Config counts: ON → OFF
409	```
410	
411	2. **Preview of HUD (Expanded layout):**
412	```
413	[Opus | Pro] │ my-project git:(main*)
414	Context ████░░░░░ 45% │ Usage ██░░░░░░░░ 25% (1h 30m / 5h)
415	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
416	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
417	```
418	
419	**Preview of HUD (Compact layout):**
420	```
421	[Opus | Pro] ████░░░░░ 45% | my-project git:(main*) | 5h: 25% | ⏱️ 5m
422	◐ Edit: file.ts | ✓ Read ×3
423	▸ Fix auth bug (2/5)
424	```
425	
426	3. **Confirm**: "Save these changes?"

428	---
429	
430	## Write Configuration
431	
432	Write to `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` inside the active config directory.
433	
434	Merge with existing config, preserving:
435	- `pathLevels` (not in configure flow)
436	- `display.usageThreshold` (advanced config)
437	- `display.environmentThreshold` (advanced config)
438	- `display.contextWarningThreshold` (advanced config)
439	- `display.contextCriticalThreshold` (advanced config)
440	- `colors` (advanced manual palette overrides)
441	
442	**Migration note**: Old configs with `layout: "default"` or `layout: "separators"` are automatically migrated to the new `lineLayout` + `showSeparators` format on load.
443	
444	### Per-config-directory overrides
445	
446	`~/.claude/claude-hud.json` (more precisely `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/claude-hud.json`) is an
447	optional overlay applied on top of `config.json` at load time. It uses the same shape,
448	only needs the keys it changes, and nested sections merge key by key:
449	
450	For example, `~/.config/claude/work/claude-hud.json` can contain:
451	
452	```json
453	{ "display": { "customLine": "Work Team" } }
454	```
455	
456	This exists for users who run several `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`s and symlink `plugins/` to one
457	shared location - `plugins/claude-hud/config.json` is then the same physical file for every
458	directory, while this overlay stays per-directory.
459	
460	Never write this file from the guided flow, and leave it untouched when it exists; it is a
461	manual escape hatch. Values in it win over anything written to `config.json`, so if a saved
462	setting appears not to take effect, check whether the overlay redefines it.
463

30	$cache = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache") -Directory | ForEach-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName "claude-hud") }) -contains $true
31	$registry = (Get-Content (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\installed_plugins.json") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -match "claude-hud"
32	$temp = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $claudeDir "plugins\cache\temp_local_*") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

37	
38	| Cache | Registry | Meaning | Action |
39	|-------|----------|---------|--------|
40	| YES | YES | Normal install (may still be broken) | Continue to Step 1 |
41	| YES | NO | Ghost install - cache orphaned | Clean up cache |
42	| NO | YES | Ghost install - registry stale | Clean up registry |
43	| NO | NO | Not installed | Continue to Step 1 |

45	If **temp files exist**, a previous install was interrupted. Clean them up.

48

50	
51	**macOS/Linux**:
52	```bash
53	CLAUDE_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
54	
55	# Remove orphaned cache (handles both direct and marketplace installs)
56	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache"/*/claude-hud
57	
58	# Remove temp files from failed installs
59	rm -rf "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/cache/temp_local_"*
60	
61	# Reset registry (removes ALL plugins - warn user first!)
62	# Only run if user confirms they have no other plugins they want to keep:
63	echo '{"version": 2, "plugins": {}}' > "$CLAUDE_DIR/plugins/installed_plugins.json"
64	```

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers — `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls.

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) — only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two — don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation — either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying — write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 4.8, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-4-8`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` — it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events

## ⚠️ API Drift — Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025–2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing — the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) — see the Server Tools QR below. |
| PHP parameter names | snake_case wire names as named args (`max_tokens`) | Top-level named args are camelCase (`maxTokens`). Nested array keys vary by feature (e.g. `'taskBudget'`, `'skillID'`, `'mcp_server_name'`) — copy the exact key from the documented example; do not bulk-convert. |
| Managed Agents credentials | Keep secrets host-side via custom tools (the only option before vaults shipped) | Vault `environment_variable` credentials — stored by Anthropic, substituted at egress, never visible in the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` → Vaults). Host-side custom tools remain the fallback for self-hosted sandboxes. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

Before reading code examples, determine which language the user is working in:

1. **Look at project files** to infer the language:
